faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and apply to award/agreement-free employees.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (e.g., annual leave, sick leave). faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the $100k salary or paid on top?

The employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings (including casual loading if applicable) into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So a $100,000 salary attracts an extra $12,000 in super, making the total employment cost $112,000.

bodyMarkdown:
## Is $100k a Good Salary in Australia?

If you’re asking “is 100k a good salary in australia”, the answer depends on your industry, experience, and whether you’re permanent or casual. A $100,000 annual salary works out to about $50.60 per hour for a 38-hour week ($100,000 ÷ 52 weeks ÷ 38 hours). That’s nearly double the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour set by the Fair Work Commission.

### How We Calculate Annual Pay

We use the standard formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. We assume a 38-hour week, which is the full-time ordinary hours under the National Employment Standards. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. For example, a $50.60 hourly rate gives:

- Weekly: $50.60 × 38 = $1,922.80
- Fortnightly: $1,922.80 × 2 = $3,845.60
- Annual: $1,922.80 × 52 = $100,000 (rounded)

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. Use our [timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see the annual equivalent.

### Comparing $100k to Australian Benchmarks

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026), which is about $108,352 per year. So $100k is slightly below that average. However, when you include all employees (including part-time and casual), total average weekly earnings are $1,579.20 ($82,118 per year). A $100k salary is well above that figure.

For casual employees, the minimum casual rate is $33.05 per hour (National Minimum Wage plus 25% loading). At $50.60 per hour, you’re earning 53% more than the minimum casual rate. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides a Pay Calculator to check award rates, which may be higher than the minimum.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

If you’re a casual employee, your employer pays a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For a $100k base salary, that would mean $125,000 in gross pay if you were casual (but note: casuals don’t get paid leave). Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to calculate this.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% from 1 July 2026. For a permanent employee earning $100,000, the employer adds $12,000 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So your total remuneration package is $112,000. For a casual earning $125,000 (including loading), super would be $15,000, making the total $140,000.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil tax on first $18,200
- 15% on $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Medicare levy is 2% (single thresholds from 2025–26 used here).

For a $100,000 salary:
- Tax: $20,520
- Medicare: $2,000
- Net annual: $77,480
- Net weekly: $1,490

Compare that to the average full-time net weekly of about $1,599 (based on $108,352 gross). Your $100k net is slightly lower, but still a comfortable income for many Australians. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to estimate your own figures.

### Award Rates and Enterprise Agreements

Most employees are covered by a modern award or enterprise agreement, which set minimum pay rates higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, a hospitality award might have higher rates for evening work. Always check your award via the Fair Work Ombudsman. If you’re award/agreement-free, the National Minimum Wage applies.

### Is $100k a Good Salary?

Yes, $100k is a good salary in Australia. It’s more than double the National Minimum Wage, above the all-employees average, and only slightly below the full-time adult average. It provides a net weekly income of about $1,490, which covers living costs in most areas. However, in expensive cities like Sydney or Melbourne, you may need to budget carefully. For context, the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page shows how $100k compares to other benchmarks.

### Super and Salary Packaging

Remember that super is paid on top. If your employer offers salary packaging (e.g., novated lease), your taxable income reduces, potentially lowering your tax. But our calculator does not deduct salary packaging, HELP repayments, or the Medicare levy surcharge. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Final Thoughts

A $100,000 salary is a strong income in Australia, especially when you factor in super and casual loading. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to see how different hourly rates stack up. And always check your award or agreement to ensure you’re being paid correctly.

*Disclaimer: Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.*
